correctness.rationale: Proposition 9 of Cai–Kiah–Nguyen–Yaakobi, arXiv:2001.01376, gives the needed if-and-only-if alternating differing interval characterization. Only even alternating intervals preserve binary Hamming weight. Cutting at equal adjacent symbols yields a unique sequence of alternating blocks; its two-state matrix gives every composition-refined degree coefficient. First-to-last mismatch endpoints make the same-weight and cross-weight edge counts disjoint and exhaustive. For each block the even-alternating interval count is the product of its symbol counts, leading to the sharp fixed-weight maximum. The density-limit proof uses the exact weight-refined edge sum and a uniform geometric bound. The direct distinct-deletion-set checker examined 698027 pairs for n=1..10; a separate matrix expansion checked all length <=24 coefficients, with independent exact histograms through n=13. These finite computations corroborate but do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The protected new invariant is the joint Hamming-weight and same-weight-degree distribution, alongside a sharp degree maximum, inter-layer edge partition and fixed-density mean. The known Type-A condition is credited rather than claimed. The closest public unrestricted degree-spectrum results and total edge census were read in full and are not equal statements: they include odd alternating intervals and aggregate away Hamming weight. The published weight-two capacity is an independence-number statement for one layer. Their stated formulas do not directly give the new trivariate distribution, though the new derivation is an economical refinement of the same interval method and remains subject to historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: The full graph pointwise degree theorem is closely related; an earlier author may have recorded the even-interval fixed-weight refinement elsewhere.
Unindexed or differently named constant-composition reconstruction enumerations could yield equivalent formulas.
No independently verified priority or mathematical audit is asserted.

value.rationale: Constant Hamming weight is a natural constraint for sparse-marker and balanced-content coding. The theorem supplies a complete all-length degree distribution, edge-layer partition, exact maximum, and fixed-density mean; these quantify local packing obstructions for source-constrained two-read reconstruction. In particular at balanced weight the mean is asymptotically 2n/3 but the maximum is n^2/4 to first order. The all-length composition-sensitive invariant is not a finite census or a reparameterization of the marginal degree histogram. No optimal codebook sizes or downstream theorems are claimed.
